items.title: Service-status presentation
items.objective: Clearly distinguish service interruptions from substantive legal replies.
items.entry: The served turn contains only service-status elements, a mixed supported reply and status, or an unconfirmed/failed save.
items.requirement: Render status-only output as a quiet accessible notice. Retain a valid saved timestamp without answer-copy or rating controls. Mixed replies retain their substantive content and source controls. Failure wording preserves the exact service reason, persistence uncertainty and the safe recovery action.
items.exit: Fresh and reopened replies display the correct notice, timestamp, controls and persistence state without changing response content or records.
items.recovery: Preserve the original brief and same-turn retry where allowed. Unconfirmed persistence stays unconfirmed; never imply saved or unsaved without evidence.
items.exclusions: Presentation only. No change to admitted evidence, response generation, release gates, saved state or model calls. No internal contract jargon in advocate-facing text.
items.acceptance: Inspect status-only, mixed supported replies, failed saves, lost acknowledgements and reopened history. Status appears once; saved timestamp remains; status-only output has no answer controls; mixed output retains source links and normal controls; safe retry remains duplicate-free.
items.dependencies: LB-182 recovery/status policy; LB-194 response contract; LB-197 qualification. Owner: nm/app/app.js::renderTurn. Reuse the existing served status elements and persistence states.

items.title: Partial recovery for missing proposal links
items.objective: Preserve independently supported work when a response unit omits a question or task association.
items.entry: An otherwise owned response unit contains an expressed question or proposed task without its required association.
items.requirement: Treat the missing association at its dependent content boundary after completing identity, source ownership, supplied-link, progress and record-outcome checks. The existing narrowed-review path may retain eligible closed evidence expressions and an honest limitation. Remove dependent proposal and progress transitions; unresolved work remains open.
items.exit: The unsupported proposal is withheld while a separately checked eligible remainder survives, with no false completion or authorised-scope expansion.
items.recovery: Use existing bounded content recovery and independent narrowed review. Preserve valid peers and accepted input. Ownership, ambiguous identity and commit-integrity failures retain their mandatory stops.
items.exclusions: No free-prose escape, inferred association, release of unchecked content, dropped source check, duplicated accepted input or larger retry bound.
items.acceptance: Pair missing associations with valid links, mixed independent units, foreign references, ambiguous ownership and exhausted recovery. Inspect the public reply, pending work, saved record and exact replay. No unlinked proposal or unsupported progress is released; checked eligible peers remain useful.
items.dependencies: LB-182 smallest-unit recovery; LB-194 closed expressions; LB-196 valid-peer preservation; LB-197 qualification. Owner: continuation.py::_validate_unit/_limited_unit/continue_conversation. Preserve execution_contracts and the turn-owned recovery ledger.
items.model_calls: No new routine stage or higher bound. Newly reachable existing narrowed-review/correction calls must be measured.

items.title: Optional retention fault isolation
items.objective: Keep a fully checked substantive rejection usable when optional salvage metadata is malformed.
items.entry: Independent response review has a valid final substantive rejection but its optional proposed retained subset fails validation.
items.requirement: Validate the core review before optional retention. Within the existing correction bound, preserve a fully checked rejection without a retained subset if the optional-only defect remains. The normal writer-correction path may continue. Keep cloud harmless-empty-metadata normalization and exact checked record outcomes.
items.exit: An optional retention fault does not erase a valid rejection, approve unread work or release any unchecked subset.
items.recovery: Use the shared recovery ledger and current reviewer/writer correction limits. Core-invalid, unread, incomplete, ambiguous and provider-failed reviews remain distinct; preserve independently checked peers.
items.exclusions: No reinterpretation of unread core review as rejection, forced acceptance, unsafe retained subset, enlarged retry budget or blanket whole-turn failure for optional metadata.
items.acceptance: Pair checked rejection plus malformed optional retention with valid retention, accepted core, invalid core, harmless empty fields, provider failure and exhausted correction. Inspect delivered work, blocked content, valid peers, service status, saved state and bounded calls through the public boundary.
items.dependencies: LB-179 validated review; LB-182 recovery; LB-194 expression/release contract; LB-197 qualification. Owner: continuation_verification.py::_decision/verify_continuation. Preserve cloud record_check, transport normalization and replay contracts.
items.model_calls: No new routine stage or higher bound. Any newly reachable existing writer replacement/recheck must be counted.

items.title: Precise private recovery diagnostics
items.objective: Make per-request failures and recovery decisions diagnosable without exposing internal processing to the advocate.
items.entry: A writer/reviewer unit fails, is corrected, is withheld or has unavailable checking.
items.requirement: Retain the owning unit, typed failure category, precise consequential mismatch and bounded recovery history in private diagnostics. Reuse exact owned references and store only necessary diagnostic evidence. Distinguish provider/service failure, unread review, semantic rejection and contract mismatch. Diagnostics never become admitted evidence or cached approval.
items.exit: Private records identify what failed and what recovery occurred; saving and replay preserve the necessary audit without altering the released reply or its evidence.
items.recovery: Preserve received checked verdicts and valid peers. Advocate-facing output remains useful requested work with task-relevant limits, or a separate truthful service status; internal recovery details stay private.
items.exclusions: No routine model call, duplicated transcript representations, public raw errors, fabricated reviewer result, diagnostic-to-evidence promotion or silent durable-schema/replay upgrade.
items.acceptance: Inspect precise unit attribution across contract, semantic and provider failures; bounded retries; partial preservation; failed saves and exact replay. Check JSON-compatible durable audit fields, privacy and unchanged response/record effects. Report call categories and attempts without treating friction counts as error rates.
items.dependencies: LB-182 recovery; LB-183 call accounting; LB-194/196 versioned evidence and recovery; LB-197 qualification. Owners: ContinuationVerification and continuation.py::continue_conversation. Discuss any inseparable audit-schema handoff before implementation.
items.model_calls: Zero new calls. Diagnostic recording does not reset the recovery ledger.

items.title: Single source selection in record review
items.objective: Remove redundant model-owned source lists while preserving canonical evidence and durable replay.
items.entry: A material or dispute reviewer selects the original sources supporting its verdict.
items.requirement: Let fresh review select sources once through validated source_checks. Code derives canonical source_ids from those checked selections. Preserve original-purpose and substantive-portion checks, scoped coverage, target ownership and current canonical saved records. Separate fresh model wire from canonical saved verdicts used by retained-review cache rereads.
items.exit: One source selection produces the same checked canonical evidence; empty, duplicate, foreign and unsupported selections cannot be admitted, and legitimate selections avoid redundant-list disagreement.
items.recovery: Preserve checked peers and bounded correction. Version or invalidate affected fresh wire/cache dependencies explicitly; historical canonical audits and exact replay remain readable without silent migration.
items.exclusions: No blind local helper copy, ambiguous source derivation, weaker support_spans/coverage checks, cache rejection of its own canonical data or revalidation of historical records under an undeclared new wire.
items.acceptance: Pair legitimate and harmless-metadata verdicts with empty, duplicate, foreign and unsupported checks. Verify material/dispute admission, source-purpose disagreement, coverage dependencies, retained cache rereads, canonical source_ids, atomic save and exact replay. Measure unnecessary rejection and conditional calls on the pinned model when separately authorised.
items.dependencies: LB-179 source/review contract; LB-182 recovery; LB-183 calls; LB-195/196 source portions/coverage; LB-197 qualification. Shared owner: record_review.py plus material/dispute verifiers, mutation_contracts and retained-review consumers. Discuss the inseparable wire/canonical/cache migration before changing files.
items.model_calls: Zero new routine calls. Retry/cost reduction is an intended benefit, not a measured claim.
